messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 4123456789 - GPU OOM surge detected in eu-west-1 during prefill. Multiple containers restarted across pool-preload-*. Autoscaling not keeping up. Paging oncall. Severity: P1.

incident-bot: Alerts: 17 OOM events in last 5m, 6 containers restarted, fallback to model-small triggered 3 times. Logs attached to incident.

amber (oncall): On it. Starting quick triage. @sre-rotation can you take memory graphs + node statuses pls?

luis: Copy. Pasting a representative container log snippet:

```
2026-03-15T02:12:31Z containerd: panic: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
...
runtime: failed to allocate heap arena
Process exited with code 137
```

luis: Seen this across 3 nodes: preload-01/02/05. All on A100-40GB. Prefill spikes from a small subset of requests with very large context.

maya: Likely long prompt + aggressive prefill combined with KV cache duplication. Quick mitigation: reduce PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS and enforce per-request max_context in gateway. Suggest: set PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048 and PREFILL_BATCH_TIMEOUT=10ms for the pool.

ryan: I can patch the deployment now. Command I will run:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/pool-preload PREFILL_MAX_TOKENS=2048 PREFILL_BATCH_TIMEOUT=10ms
kubectl rollout restart deployment/pool-preload
```

amber (oncall): Do it. Also enable immediate fallback to quantized-v2 for new requests to reduce mem. How many customers are impacted?

product-support: We're tracking 3 customers with high long-context usage (acct-A, acct-B, acct-C). We'll prepare a short note after we have ETA.

sre-rotation: Grafana link: https://grafana.internal/r/ooms?panel=mem-usage - memory spike aligns with long-context request bursts at 02:09-02:14 UTC. Node prefill-02 shows steady increase in GPU memory then crash. Watching.

ryan: Patch applied and rolled, restart completed on pool-preload (3/3 updated). Verifying logs now.

ops-bot: Rolling restart started by ryan at 02:18 UTC. All pods reported Ready by 02:20 UTC.

luis: After restart we see reduced OOMs but one pod ephemeral OOM during warmup. I toggled eviction threshold to be more aggressive: set GPU_EVICTION_THRESHOLD=0.85 on pool-preload.

maya: Also flipped prefix caching off for the pool to avoid duplicated KV caching: set PREFILL_CACHE_ENABLED=false. That should stop duplicated memory growth for long requests.

amber (oncall): Good. Monitoring for 30m. If stable, we downgrade to P2. @product-support prepare customer message: what happened, what we did, and recommended short-term mitigation (reduce max_context, use quantized fallback).

product-support: Draft: "We experienced GPU OOMs impacting prefill for long-context requests in eu-west-1 between ~02:09-02:22 UTC. We applied config changes (reduced prefill max tokens, disabled prefill cache) and rolled the pool. Most customers recovered immediately; a small set saw retries. We recommend lowering per-request max context or using quantized model variants until we ship a permanent fix." Will send once amber approves.

sre-rotation: Alerting automation also created a follow-up ticket to add guardrails: reject requests > 64k tokens on this pool and add request size histogram.

amber (oncall): Assigning postmortem to luis. Please include root-cause, why autoscaler didn't compensate, and a permanent fix plan (runtime KV dedupe, request-size throttles, improved heuristics). Postmortem due EOD tomorrow.

luis: Ack. I'll start collecting logs/traces and timeline.

amber (oncall): Thanks team. Leaving monitoring to @sre-rotation. If we see recurrence escalate to infra lead.

incident-bot: Incident 4123456789 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Created follow-up: INC-4123457 (postmortem).

product-support: Customer note sent at 02:42 UTC to affected accounts.

amber (oncall): Closing this thread for active ops, will reopen if memory trend rises. :white_check_mark:
